trends.name: Iran-US Strait of Hormuz Crisis
trends.summary: Trump has issued a 26-hour deadline for Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz following military escalations, with reports of explosions in Bandar Abbas near key Iranian military sites. NATO is coordinating a response to potentially reopen the strait, creating acute geopolitical risk that's triggering broad risk-off sentiment across equities and crypto markets.

trends.name: Market Sell-Off & Recession Odds Spike
trends.summary: Asia markets (Kospi, Nikkei) fell >5%, S&P 500 futures flat, Bitcoin below $68,000, and recession odds jumped to 36.9% amid Iran escalation and broader risk-off sentiment. Markets are pricing in heightened uncertainty from geopolitical tensions and potential economic headwinds.

trends.name: US Housing Market Collapse
trends.summary: New home sales fell 17.6% MoM in January to 587,000 units (lowest since 2022) and 11.3% YoY, marking the worst annual decline in 3 years and far exceeding expectations. This signals severe demand destruction in a critical economic sector and potential leading indicator for broader slowdown.

trends.name: TSA Staffing & Airport Security Overhaul
trends.summary: Trump is deploying ICE agents to airports to support TSA operations on March 27 amid staffing shortages, facing criticism from lawmakers over civil liberties and safety concerns. This signals operational stress in critical transportation infrastructure amid potential government shutdown deadline.

trends.name: Semiconductor & AI Chip Sector Strength
trends.summary: Micron and AMD face mixed signals as AI demand remains strong but macroeconomic headwinds create uncertainty. OpenAI's pivot to large data center spending is raising Wall Street IPO valuation concerns, while Super Micro faces optics challenges. Sector remains critical to market performance but faces valuation pressure.

trends.name: Energy & Commodity Price Volatility
trends.summary: Oil and energy prices face acute upside risk from Strait of Hormuz closure threat, while gold mining stocks are positioned as a hedge. Natural gas services and energy infrastructure plays are benefiting from geopolitical premium, though tariff concerns are pressuring broader commodity inflation.

trends.name: Tariffs & Consumer Price Inflation
trends.summary: Inflation in imported goods is accelerating across pineapples, plastic, chocolate, berries, and menstrual products due to tariffs and global supply chain pressure. Consumers face higher prices and reduced purchasing power, adding to economic headwind concerns and retail demand weakness.

trends.name: Private Credit & Fixed Income Risk
trends.summary: Advisors are cautioning on private credit exposure amid economic uncertainty and rising recession risks, while high-yield fund commentary suggests selective positioning. New Zealand yields hit 1-year highs signaling global rate pressure, and municipal bond funds face mixed outlook.

trends.name: China Economic Challenges & Trade Surplus
trends.summary: China's Premier is addressing rising trade surplus amid export surge, signaling potential trade tensions. Emotional economy trends in consumer spending contrast with underlying economic weakness, creating mixed signals on Chinese demand and its impact on US exporters.

trends.name: Tech & Streaming Platform Disruption
trends.summary: Netflix's cooking show content is driving unexpected 303% booking jumps at restaurants, demonstrating streaming's influence on consumer behavior and offline commerce. Spotify's AI integration strategy is critical to subscriber retention amid competition, signaling evolving value propositions in media.

trends.name: Healthcare & Demographics as Growth Driver
trends.summary: Aging population continues to fuel healthcare hiring and demand even amid broader economic weakness, with Incyte positioned as undervalued. Healthcare sector shows relative resilience and offers defensive positioning against macroeconomic headwinds.

trends.name: Wealth Inequality & Political Economic Tensions
trends.summary: Bernie Sanders highlights extreme wealth concentration—Elon Musk holds more wealth than bottom 53% of households—raising questions about economic sustainability and potential policy responses. This reflects growing political focus on inequality that could influence regulatory and tax policy direction.
